clue.text: Musically fine — big sounds

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how a word is said out loud, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: big means fat, and the slang word is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: A music critic praising a piece that sounds grand and full.
explanation.definitionFit: Phat is slang praise for excellent music, especially hip-hop, so 'musically fine' is a fair gloss.

clue.text: Plainest male developed a heavenly body?

indicators.note: developed means changed or worked into a new form

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The most ordinary-looking man grew into a gorgeous hunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' looks like praise of a physique; the question mark admits it is astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetesimal is a small solid body in space that clumped with others to form planets.

clue.text: Temple in which bird protects egg

indicators.note: protects means shields by enclosing, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a heron is a wading bird
O is egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A temple where a bird guards its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroon is a temple or shrine dedicated to a hero in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Symbol shows Turkish officer embracing maiden

indicators.note: embracing means holding something within its arms

blocks.note: an aga was a Turkish commander
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An emblem showing a Turkish officer hugging a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Agma is the phonetic character used for the ng sound, a symbol.

clue.text: Bones of saint — any number gathered in time

indicators.note: gathered in means collected inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: St is short for saint
an era is a period of time
n stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A saint's relics, of which any number are collected over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone, so bones.

clue.text: Sheep not totally domesticated going at full speed?

indicators.note: not totally means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: rams are male sheep
tame means domesticated

explanation.surface: A half-wild sheep careering about the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramstam is a Scots word meaning headlong or rash; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramstam describes rushing headlong without care, which is moving at full tilt.

clue.text: Wander in race

blocks.note: first meaning: a dialect verb, to stray about
second meaning: a white streak down a horse's face, also spelt rache

explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' is not a contest but the white blaze on a horse's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives this word both as a dialect verb to rove and as a variant of race, a horse's facial blaze.

clue.text: Motorway — one when meeting another one creates foul atmosphere

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one
as means when
another motorway, meeting the first

explanation.surface: Where one motorway meets another, the air turns foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasm, or miasma, is a noxious vapour or unwholesome atmosphere.

clue.text: Endlessly harsh friend dealt with on an individual basis

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

blocks.note: severe means harsh
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend who is constantly harsh is dealt with one to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally means separately or each in turn, as in jointly and severally liable.

clue.text: As before, to terrify with rage is wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and must be put right

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Frightening people with anger is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrise is an obsolete verb meaning to horrify or terrify, hence 'as before'.

clue.text: Underground workers carrying new ensign — they would wax lyrical

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the word is reformed in a different order
carrying means bearing something within

blocks.note: miners work underground
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Coal miners parading a fresh flag break into song.
explanation.walkthrough: Minnesingers were medieval German lyric poets and singers of courtly love.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesingers composed and sang love lyrics, so they would wax lyrical in the literal sense.

clue.text: Beneficiaries, say, coming into foreign money, meeting stars

indicators.note: coming into means one piece enters inside the other

blocks.note: the lat was the currency of Latvia
e.g. means for example, 'say'
Aries is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: Heirs who come into money from abroad and meet celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: The lat was Latvia's currency before the euro, which is why it counts as foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Legataries are legatees, people who receive a legacy under a will, so they are beneficiaries.

clue.text: Band in play heading off to entertain king

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed
to entertain is to take someone in, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's play
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A band in a stage production loses its leader but entertains a king.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMLET loses its H to give AMLET, and R goes inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band worn around the arm.

clue.text: Cleric rolling over in function in pub

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round so it reads the other way
in places this piece inside the other

blocks.note: tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function
Rev. is short for Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A drunken vicar rolling about at a function held in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house where drink is served.

clue.text: The reverse of excellent, gross, rum

indicators.note: the reverse of means read backwards

blocks.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
gross means fat

explanation.surface: Something the opposite of excellent: disgusting and odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective meaning odd, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tafia is a type of cheap West Indian rum distilled from molasses.

clue.text: One of the learned folk, true A-list nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A scholar who is genuinely a crazy celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A literatus is a man of letters, one of the literati, the learned class.

clue.text: Like some packages with crumpled marks about to be dumped

indicators.note: to be dumped means these letters are thrown out of the word

blocks.note: bearing crumpled marks is being creased
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Parcels arrive crumpled and are about to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RE out of CREASED to leave CASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Packages that are cased are enclosed in a case or box.

clue.text: Stain of English wickedness, nothing being admitted

indicators.note: being admitted means let in, so this piece goes inside

blocks.note: E is short for English
O looks like zero, nothing
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A moral stain on the English character, with nothing let in to excuse it.
explanation.walkthrough: O is let in between E and SIN. 'Stain' looks moral here but it is the dye used in microscopy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red dye used as a stain for microscope slides.

clue.text: Cunning employer, last character to come forward

indicators.note: the final letter is moved from the end up to the front of the word

blocks.note: one who employs something is its user

explanation.surface: A crafty boss, whose last worker is told to step forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruse as a noun is a trick or piece of cunning.

clue.text: As battle is raging these populations are preserved

indicators.note: raging suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: While war rages, some groups of people are kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The populations are of micro-organisms, not people; a stabilate is a population of organisms preserved in a viable state, typically frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stabilate is a sample population of micro-organisms kept frozen for later use, i.e. preserved.

clue.text: Muslim woman to ask for charity with hesitation

blocks.note: to beg is to ask for alms
um is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A woman hesitantly asks for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: A begum is a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia, a lady.

clue.text: How angels act no longer easy? You mean that?

blocks.note: ethe is an obsolete word for easy
'Really?' asks whether someone is serious

explanation.surface: A doubter questioning whether angels still have it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels are spirits, airy and heavenly, so they behave ethereally.

clue.text: Sticking out against wine

blocks.note: to means against, as in cheek to cheek
rosé is pink wine

explanation.surface: Someone standing out by opposing wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Torose means bulging or knobbly, swelling out in protuberances.

clue.text: Gloomy appearance that is associated with bird

blocks.note: a lour is a frowning, threatening look
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A bird whose sombre look is all anyone notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A lourie is a turaco, a brightly coloured African bird.

clue.text: Old traveller in pain, having very little money

blocks.note: gip, or gyp, is pain
a sen is a tiny coin of Japan and elsewhere

explanation.surface: An elderly wanderer suffering and nearly penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Gipsen is a Spenserian form of gypsy, an archaic word for a travelling person.

clue.text: See young hawk no longer fly high

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete spelling of sore, a hawk in its first year, as a dictionary 'see' entry
second meaning: to rise high in the air

explanation.surface: Watch a young bird of prey take off and climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the dictionary's cross-reference: Chambers lists this spelling as an obsolete form, with 'see' pointing to the hawk entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to rise or glide high in the air; the old noun spelling meant a first-year hawk.

clue.text: Actor in Macbeth, especially

indicators.note: in means the word lies inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: letters that straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A performer, particularly in the Scottish play.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesp is a short informal form of thespian, an actor.

clue.text: Baddies overthrown, knight being luminary in Scotland

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the word is read upwards

blocks.note: rats are nasty people
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: Villains toppled, a knight becomes a Scottish celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Starn is a Scots word for a star, a shining body in the sky.

clue.text: 'orrible place surrounded by chemical

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in 'orrible tells us to drop the opening H the same way

blocks.note: a hole is a place, as in a grim little hole
being in something is being surrounded by it

explanation.surface: A cockney grumbling about a horrible spot hemmed in by chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Olein is a glyceride of oleic acid, a chemical compound found in fats and oils.

clue.text: Cabinet in academy with temporary accommodation?

blocks.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is the degree of someone in academia
a hut is makeshift shelter

explanation.surface: A cupboard in a school that is housed in a prefab.
explanation.definitionFit: A bahut is an ornamental cabinet or chest, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Gentile standing on head, one participant in spiritual discipline

indicators.note: standing on one's head turns things upside down, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

blocks.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A non-Jew doing a headstand during yoga practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi practises yoga, a spiritual and physical discipline.

clue.text: Card game with money, Eton pursuit once

blocks.note: monte is a Spanish-American card game
M is short for money

explanation.surface: Gambling at cards for cash, a pastime once enjoyed at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the English boarding school; Montem was its old custom of collecting money from passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Montem was a former Eton College custom of processing to a mound and levying 'salt money' from passers-by.

clue.text: Rock king embraced by a girl

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
Rose is a girl's name
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A rock star king hugged by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes inside A ROSE, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkose is a type of sandstone rich in feldspar, so a rock.

clue.text: A superior type of journalist who hunts with a bird?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a person, with the leading A belonging to the wordplay

blocks.note: taken as written
U means upper-class
a stringer is a freelance local correspondent

explanation.surface: A posh reporter who goes hawking in his spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: An austringer is a falconer who keeps goshawks, hunting with a trained hawk.

clue.text: At least three members showing cricket technique

blocks.note: plural limbs, the first of at least three
pin is slang for a leg, the further member

explanation.surface: Several limbs on display as part of a cricketing skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is slang for legs, so LEGS plus PIN makes at least three legs. Leg spin is spin bowling that turns the ball from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is a style of bowling in cricket where the wrist imparts turn, so a technique.

clue.text: In fit of temper these containers are knocked over

definitions.note: plural noun phrase standing for the answer

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so the word reads the other way

blocks.note: a snit is a fit of pique

explanation.surface: In a tantrum, someone knocks over a pile of cans.
explanation.definitionFit: Tins are metal cans, so they are containers.
